scope: Ground-first alpine grassland, shared savanna brush geometry and atlas, regional flower illustrations; no tree/camera/terrain/light/sky change.

visualCritiqueFirst.observation: Thin isolated grass strips compete with a smooth undetailed ground surface.
Foreground lacks continuous soft vegetation masses and parallax.
Regional flower fields should read as coherent botanical shapes, not repeated polygonal spikes.

artisticHypothesis: Transfer broad ground values, root-matched painterly tuft cards and selected dimensional accents from savanna to a green alpine meadow, with clustered regional flower cards.

techniques.ground: New generated meadow albedo; mirrored wrap, sRGB, mipmaps, anisotropy8, world6m scale and macro colours.
techniques.grass: Shared savanna brushGeometry(true,true,1.45) and original atlas, recoloured by the meadow pigment field. Existing low clumps use shared curved reedGeometry.
techniques.flowers: Four padded illustrated tiles: paintbrush, violet fleabane, white western-anemone and pale fleabane variation. Three semantic forms in one instanced batch.
techniques.rootMatching: Ground and plants share macro pigments; projected ground detail fades above6–30cm; terrain normals transferred after rock clearance.
techniques.placement: Inherited grass count, existing flower banks plus6 irregular middle-distance drifts, isolated flower marks removed; slope/rock/drainage checks remain.

regionalEvidence.evidenceUsed: Parks Canada search-indexed guide text names paintbrush, western anemone and fleabanes. Direct full PDF retrieval timed out. No external imagery downloaded.

rounds.evidence: Better ground/flower silhouettes; grass too low, reed accents nearly black.
Taller brush gives more body, but vertical streaks remain. Normals corrected for dimensional accents.
Root-normal transfer alone barely changes streaks. Isolated tuft/shader inspection confirms world-projected ground detail stretched up cards; height-fading that detail markedly improves integration.

technicalCorrections: Move macro math from fragment to vertex

performanceInvestigation.actualOutcome: Macro baking preserves appearance but does not remove the slowdown. Fixed-camera ablations localize most added cost to the brush layer.
